Not great
Sep 2026 • Couples

Starter drunken chicken was cold and inedible however main courses were better. When we went to pay the server insisted my husband sign up to Marriott to get a discount, however this was a long process and seems to be part of their role as quite insistent. Has to be tons of other better Cantonese restaurants in HCMC so I would give this a miss

Once again, thank you for your constructive feedback. We hope to have the opportunity to welcome you back in the future for a more enjoyable dining experience.

reviews.review_text:
Meander23398583831
1 contribution
0
Food poisoning after dining at Libai!!!
Aug 2025 • Family
Last Sunday (August 24), my family (8 adults and 2 kids, both 7 years old) had a joint birthday celebration for my husband and my two older brothers with a reservation at 6:30 PM. We ordered quite a lot of dishes, including the Peking duck served two ways: duck skin rolls and duck fried rice.

My first impression was that the duck skin rolls were very crispy and flavorful. However, when it came to the fried rice, the duck meat tasted dry and had a strange smell. Still, since the rice was cooked with many toppings like cucumber, mushrooms, bell peppers, and seasoned heavily (especially with ginger), I assumed it was just the way the dish was meant to taste. The bill that night was over 6 million VND, and I used the Visa Signature program.

Later that night, I started feeling off — bloated and kept burping up the taste of the food. I couldn’t eat anything the entire next day, and after coming home from work in the evening, I had a full-blown combo of diarrhea and vomiting, repeatedly, until I’d thrown up everything I ate the night before. Honestly, I wouldn’t have blamed the restaurant if it weren’t for the fact that all I threw up was clearly duck fried rice with all the toppings (gross but true — just thinking about it while writing this makes me nauseous again). More concerning — both of my older brothers also had the exact same symptoms. 

I ended up having to take two days off work and could only eat plain porridge during that time. To this day, this has been the worst food poisoning experience I’ve ever had — and it came from a supposedly reputable restaurant inside a 5-star hotel. If this had happened at a street food stall, I wouldn’t even bother writing a review (FYI, I’ve never had food poisoning from any street food in Saigon).

I contacted the restaurant to inform them of the incident, and their response was to ask what we had eaten in the three days before followed by a request to fill out a food safety form and submit it to the restaurant. Checked their Google reviews and turns out there are tons of 1-star ratings already.

This is a real review so y’all can have one more reason NOT to eat at Libai — especially avoid the Peking duck. Even if I were invited, I wouldn’t go back.
I’d rate it below zero if that were possible — absolutely not worthy of being called a dining experience.

reviews.review_text:
Irene Eng
Tampa, Florida6163 contributions
0
Elegant and delicious
Dec 2024 • Couples
Definitely will return.

The chilli paste!!!

Love their simple and elegant decor, even the menu is beautifully bounded. The service is on the spot. Presentation is beautiful and appetizing.

Li Bai (701-62) was one of top poets of China. Kids in China grow up with his poems.

The restaurant offers more than Cantonese cuisine. I’m so looking forward to an authentic Cantonese dinner, so we went.

Our bellies could only take two dishes:
Steamed cod: most wonderful.
Dongpo Pork 东坡肉: the meat is tender, dish is tasty and well presented but it’s not the traditional dongpo. The color of the meat is too light and dull, and tasted different. I was expecting the deep and shiny square pork belly, often served strings tied like a gift box. The mahogany color is from caramelized rock sugar. I don’t like my food sweet but this is one of few dishes that I don’t mind.

The freebies are delicious: tiny fried anchovy with the chilli sauce, and cashews. Their hot sauce is the best during my three weeks trip, hands down. What a treat! When I mention this to the young lady, she said sweetly “I can give you some to take home.”I wasn’t going to but after she refilled it toward end of the meal, I said, “ok.” since they’ll threw it away. … AND I shared it with my friends the following morning, and we finished it - we’re dying for a good chilli paste. I’ve two bowls of pho, seriously, all because of this.

Wish their ceiling could be a bit higher. Being on the third floor in the Sheraton, this will never happen.

We didn’t order dessert… because I want my durian -:)

Mar 2022 • Family
Libai Restaurant is inside Sheraton Hotel in Saigon. I have been here twice and for both times, I was totally impressed by the waiting staff’s professional manner and friendly attitude.

This time, I went to Libai with my family to celebrate my hubby’s birthday on Sunday afternoon. As usual, the waitress Nhi and other staff were very accommodating and responsive to us during our dining time. There is a wide range of dim sum here and all of them are top-notch since they are made by Cantonese chefs. We decided to have dim sum buffet for 5 people since we wanted to try as many types of dim sum as possible, but next time, I think I’ll stick with a-la-carte 😂😂😂 because there’s no way I can stuff all of those yummy dumplings in my stomach in just one meal. All of the dumplings are out-of-the-world with very thin skin and high-quality fillings, like you can really bite a shrimp contained in a dumpling. Bamboo charcoal dumplings, salted egg custard steam buns and egg tarts are MUST-TRY. I swear Never in other Chinese restaurants have I had such a heavenly taste when eating egg tarts. My parents still keep talking about how savory and beautiful those dumplings are. 

I will certainly come back to try other dishes.

reviews.review_text:
Chris W
London, United Kingdom15 contributions
0
Bitter sweet
Dec 2018 • Couples
They have ok selection of gin but for £10 for a single, however served with not great tonic & when asked for a slice of lemon they only had lime. Meal for 2, you can only order a whole roast duck.. no middle ground for individual or smaller portions. Seems they have the menu tailored more for larger groups. 
Misleading website saying “50 varieties of dim sum”, but this is lunch only & we were disappointed to see only a few available for dinner. Secondly ALL dim sum are cooked in pork fat, so if you can’t eat pork like us you will struggle to enjoy this. 

It was very expensive for Vietnam, but cheaper than a top restaurant in the UK.
The food we ordered was very tasty, we had chicken cartilage, shredded beef, seafood fried rice, prawn vermicelli noodles. 
We were really disappointed about the dim sum but Lam tran was excellent serving us.

Not the best char siu pork we have had in Vietnam, but good service and atmosphere.
Nov 2018 • Couples
Now it is time to complete our own survey of the char siu (BBQ pork) in the three cities we have had. Sorry to say that the char siu in Novotel in Da Nang is still the best, we would rank it second place here in Sheraton in Ho Chi Minh City, and then third in Pan Pacific in Hanoi.

It is a dish that we usually order to mark the quality of the cantonese restaurants. Li Bai does it fine, but lacks the melting sensation, and the cutting is a bit thick.

And now I probably do not recommend cantonese chefs to put the gong bao chicken in the menu, because it seems like an interpretation of the dish, rather than with the original ingredients. Li Bai also does it fine with cashew nuts, but probably it should be named differently.

However, don't get me wrong. We still had a good dinner in Li Bai. We especially appreciate the service and the atmosphere.

Good enough...
Dec 2018 • Couples
I have been trying out different restaurants in Saigon looking for Hong Kong style dimsum, and this place is the best compared to others in similar price range, but...it's just good enough when factoring in everything such as selection, service...price.

It's part of the tradition and habit to drink tea with dimsum as it helps to cut the greasy feel and to cleanse the palate. The most popular tea is PuErh (BoLay) among the Chinese and the good ones are expensive. I expected a decent brew that's consistent with the price of the dimsum, but what was served is no different than tap water.

When I inquired about different PuErh as I was willing to pay more for some good tea to go with the dimsum, and I was told by the head waitress "this is all we serve...our customers bring their own tea." ...Hmmm...

Some may say that this is nitpicking, but when you spent the equivalent of a third of monthly salary of the locals for a meal for 2 people, you expect the best, not just good enough.

reviews.review_text:
Christopher L
Hewitt, New Jersey950 contributions
0
Excellent food and excellent service
Jul 2018 • Family
I guess compared to other places this is expensive but we ordered a lot of food for the six of us and our bill was under two hundred bucks. The service was very good from being greeted when we walked in though the entire meal. I think the prices are reasonable. 

The Peking duck was excellent - they prepared the roll up duck table side. They also made us duck fried rice with the extra, some made it back to the Hotel. They would have also served the duck with noodles or vegetables if we wanted. 

The dim sum selection is limited to only six items, but the four we chose was excellent. My teenagers and their two friends loved the pork buns, I loved the other dumplings. 

The sweet and sour chicken was not deep fried and heavily breaded like I am used to in Chinatown in Flushing or Manhattan NY USA - this was much better tasting. The chicken was tender, lightly breaded, and the sauce was delicious and not thick and pasty. 

We also shared the ginger chicken with scallions - another excellent dish. We shared a calamari and shrimp entree and two bowls of fried wonton soup. Everything was excellent. We chose large sizes on everything when offered and we all shared. 

The Sheraton lobby is a “back to the future” ride to the 1980’s and the restaurant decor is not much better, but everything is meticulously maintained and clean which made the dated appearance ok. We were here to eat and I’m glad we chose Li Bai restaurant for Chinese food.

Wonderful food & friendly staff
Jun 2018 • Couples
My boyfriend and I came here for dinner on our last night in Vietnam. We had the pleasure of being served by Kheng Le who was very polite and made sure he did all he could to provide a pleasant dining experience. The hard working Vietnamese work ethic was clear in his service and made us feel at ease in this foreign country.

The food was also delicious. We had BBQ pork buns, prawn pan fried dumplings, wonton soup, Sweet and sour pork, wok fried lemon grass chicken and veggie fried rice. All of the food was delicious and fresh!! I’m a pretty picky eater so eating in Vietnam was difficult for me a times but this was a meal I was fully able to enjoy with no reservations.

They also provided a 15% discount for being SPG gold members. Our meal ended up being about $75 total and we ordered enough for four people. 

Overall a great experience and would definitely consider dining here again in Saigon in the future.

reviews.review_text:

Darwin38 contributions
0
Santa came to lunch
Dec 2016 • Friends
A five star restaurant in a five star hotel with five star service.

It was Christmas Day and the several venues in which we attempted to book, were all fully booked. And the main restaurant here said they could set a table for us, but it was tucked away from the Buffet. We opted for their Li Bai Chinese Restaurant upstairs, one more floor, which offered a special menu for the day. Christmas fare with Vietnamese flair.

Absolutely delicious. The fresh ingredients were cooked to a turn presented attractively and served with impeccable joy. The extensive drinks list, gave a wide range of options to suit every palate and purse. The maitre d seemed to take great delight in serving our table and made us feel pretty special

During our meal, there was a slight pause in serving our next choices, and the reason soon enthralled us. A group of young people, who were appropriately dressed in the theme, for the occasion, complete with the necessary headgear, entertained the diners with a selection of Carols. The choir was accompanied by a person on a keyboard and a portly gentleman imitating the Grand Old Fella. Their bracket of Christmas favourites were very well received by the diners who showed their appreciation with long and loud applause.
What a pleasant interlude.

What more could we expect for Christmas. A very tasty lunch in perfect surroundings with top service and complemented by a choir. Everywhere we looked, reminded us of the festive season. I should add that the foyer had a giant Christmas tree and snowman. Yes, we took a few happy snaps, as did many others.

We were replete after a delicious lunch and feeling very satisfied with the whole day. Our aim, was for the five of us to celebrate Christmas, but our yummy lunch was distracted by constant reminders of the theme for the day.
We were blessed that Santa could come to lunch.

I should add that we have enjoyed the culinary delights served in the Li bai, previously. And we will certainly dine there again. I do not usually review five star establishments, as they invariably promote themselves, by having five stars. They are not everyday places for the average tourist huh?

Might be the best Dim Sum in HCMC but nothing special compared to elsewhere
Jun 2012 • Couples
Okay I went there on the rave reviews that I've read here and went with the Dim Sum Buffet so that I could get broad selection. Firstly keep in mind as I was only in HCMC for 2 weeks my Dim Sum cravings were not at the point where I'd eat anything remotely Dim Sum and think it was the food of the gods. 

So saying all that I can only say that the Dim Sum here was average and with non-alcoholic drinks floating around the 120,000 dong mark and the buffet itself going for 580,000 dong and adding on service charge and tax I was paying something like 850,000 dong for a pretty average meal. You know one of those Dim Sum buffets where everything ends up tasting kind of the same? That's how it was for me. I was still hungry at the end but couldn't face stomaching more of the same - not that it was bad - I just needed something different.

All up I wouldn't go here again. I'd just wait until I was in Singapore, Hong Kong or even Bangkok or Australia to get my Dim Sum.

If you're a long term expat in need of Dim Sum then by all means try it out but if you're just passing through don't bother.

Luxury Yum Cha
Apr 2012 • Family
This second floor restaurant was a cool haven on a hot day. Having immersed ourselves in the street food of Vietnam, we took a time-out for a little luxury, and something semi-familiar for the kids. They thought they knew yum cha from home, but this place opened their eyes and palates to yum cha on a whole new level. No cheerful waiters pushing steam carts, this was a la carte and presented by the most beautiful staff clad in chic silk cheongsams. We ate steamed dumplings, vegetables, and the inevitable pork bun, but the hero of our table was a dish of fat noodles and beef that had us in a chopstick frenzy as we scooped up the marvelously rich and smoky morsels. This dish is Highly Recommended.

The service was perfect. The decor is very lush in the expected East meets West luxury hotel mould. The menu is expansive, the food superior, and the styling and presentation of dishes was immaculate. Yet, amazingly, four of us ate very very well for under AU$50 !
